sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: As we wrote this script, wildfires were ripping through Northern California,
sentences.zh: 在我们写下这篇稿子时，野火正肆虐加利福尼亚州北部，

sentences.en: burning millions of acres and filling our beautiful city with smoke.
sentences.zh: 烧毁了数百万英亩的土地，并将我们美丽的城市填满浓烟。

sentences.en: At the same time, across the country, a massive tropical storm bore down on the Gulf Coast,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在全国范围内，一场威力巨大的热带风暴正逼近墨西哥湾沿岸，

sentences.en: and Phoenix, Arizona recorded its 50th day of the year above 110 degrees.
sentences.zh: 而亚利桑那州菲尼克斯市记录了今年第50个气温超过110华氏度的日子。

sentences.en: We know that these stories are connected to a bigger story,
sentences.zh: 我们知道这些报道都与一个更大的故事紧密相连，

sentences.en: and honestly, trying to keep on top of all the bad climate news can be unbearably depressing.
sentences.zh: 说实话，试图跟进所有关于气候的负面新闻可能会让人感到压抑得无法呼吸。

sentences.en: They're the kind of headlines that make you want to just not click.
sentences.zh: 这类新闻标题往往让你只想直接关掉网页。

sentences.en: And so, when it seems like there's a piece of genuinely good environmental news,
sentences.zh: 因此，当似乎出现一条真正的好消息时——关于环境的，

sentences.zh: 我总是会疯狂点开那个链接。

sentences.zh: 这位是制作人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: Solar power prices at an all-time low.
sentences.zh: 太阳能发电价格创下历史新低。

sentences.en: Endangered tigers making a comeback.
sentences.zh: 濒危老虎数量实现回升。

sentences.en: ExxonMobil doing so poorly, it gets taken off the Dow Jones.
sentences.zh: 埃克森美孚表现糟糕，被移出道琼斯指数。

sentences.en: And one morning, in the summer of 2019, right after the warmest June in the history of Junes,
sentences.zh: 就在2019年夏天的一个早晨，紧接着有史以来最热的六月之后，

sentences.en: I got a surprise dopamine hit when I saw this headline.
sentences.zh: 当我看到这个标题时，我获得了一剂意外的多巴胺冲击。

sentences.en: Tree planting has mind-blowing potential to tackle climate crisis.
sentences.zh: 植树对于应对气候危机具有令人惊叹的潜力。

sentences.en: Now, to be perfectly clear, the most mind-blowing thing we could do to tackle the climate crisis
sentences.zh: 现在，为了说得更明白一点，我们为应对气候危机能做的最令人惊叹的事情

sentences.en: is to stop burning fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 就是停止燃烧化石燃料。

sentences.en: But there are also ways that we can soak up some of the CO2 that we've already put into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 但我们也可以通过其他方式吸收一部分已经排放到大气中的二氧化碳。

sentences.en: We're developing machines to do this, but trees and other plants actually do it naturally.
sentences.zh: 我们正在研发这样做的机器，但树木和其他植物实际上是以自然方式做到这一点的。

sentences.en: They take in carbon from the atmosphere and store it in their leaves and branches and trunks.
sentences.zh: 它们吸收大气中的碳，并将其储存在叶子、树枝和树干中。

sentences.en: And so some scientists in Switzerland tried to calculate how much carbon could be removed
sentences.zh: 因此，瑞士的一些科学家试图计算出可以消除多少碳

sentences.en: if we planted as many trees as possible all around the world.
sentences.zh: 如果我们真能在全世界尽可能多地植树。

sentences.en: They published a paper in the journal Nature arguing that if humans planted a trillion trees,
sentences.zh: 他们在《自然》杂志上发表了一篇论文，提出如果人类种植一万亿棵树，

sentences.en: it could remove one-third of all the CO2 we had put up there in the first place.
sentences.zh: 它就可以消除我们最初排放到大气中的所有二氧化碳的三分之一。

sentences.en: It was a dramatic finding that led to a lot of dramatic headlines.
sentences.zh: 这是一个戏剧性的发现，引发了许多耸人听闻的头条新闻。

sentences.en: And the way the paper was being described, you would think that trees were some kind of climate change panacea,
sentences.zh: 从这篇论文被描述的方式来看，你会以为树木是某种气候变化的灵丹妙药，

sentences.en: that they were the key to fixing global warming.
sentences.zh: 认为它们是解决全球变暖的关键。

sentences.en: And in the months that followed, it felt like the tree planting theory was being aggressively put into practice.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，植树造林的理论似乎被积极地付诸实践。

sentences.en: Plant a tree to fight the effects of fossil fuels.
sentences.zh: 种下一棵树，对抗化石燃料的影响。

sentences.en: We start in Ethiopia, where a huge campaign has been launched to plant more than 4 billion trees this summer.
sentences.zh: 我们从埃塞俄比亚开始，那里今年夏天发起了一场种植超过40亿棵树的大型运动。

sentences.en: Not volunteers in India planted more than 66 million trees in just 12 hours in a record-breaking...
sentences.zh: 印度的志愿者在短短12小时内打破记录种植了超过6600万棵树……

sentences.en: There's even a tree planting anthem.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一首植树赞歌。

sentences.en: Eventually, the tree planting gospel found the unlikeliest of champions.
sentences.zh: 最终，植树造林的福音找到了最意想不到的支持者。

sentences.en: President Donald Trump expressed his love of tree planting at the World Economic Forum.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统在世界经济论坛上表达了他对植树的热爱。

sentences.en: And then Trump, the man who pulled the U.S.
sentences.zh: 接着，这个退出了巴黎气候条约的男人——特朗普，

sentences.en: out of the Paris Climate Treaty,
sentences.zh: 签署了一项名为“一万亿棵树倡议”的计划。

sentences.en: signed on to something called the Trillion Trees Initiative.
sentences.zh: 在地球日，特朗普总统在白宫草坪上召集了媒体，观看他亲手种下一棵树。

sentences.en: On Earth Day, President Trump gathered the press on the White House lawn to watch him plant a tree of his own.
sentences.zh: 作为我们奉献精神的标志，片刻之后，

sentences.en: As a sign of our dedication in a few moments,
sentences.zh: 第一夫人和我就要在这里的白宫南草坪上种下一棵枫树。

sentences.en: the First Lady and I will plant a maple tree right here on the south lawn of the White House.
sentences.zh: 这棵树在哪儿，这棵树现在在哪儿？

sentences.en: Wherever the tree is, where is this tree now?
sentences.zh: 这是一根漂亮的直树干。

sentences.en: That's a beautiful straight trunk.
sentences.zh: 这是一棵AAA级的树。

sentences.en: That's a AAA tree.
sentences.zh: AAA级的树已经种在地里了。

sentences.en: The AAA tree was already in the ground.
sentences.zh: 但总统、第一夫人和内阁成员们拿起他们的金铲子，往洞里铲了一些泥土。

sentences.en: But the president, the first lady, members of cabinet, picked up their golden shovels and threw some dirt in the hole.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 我干得很好。

sentences.en: I'm very good.
sentences.zh: 这非常好。

sentences.en: It's very good.
sentences.zh: 现在，请别误解我的意思。

sentences.en: Now, don't get me wrong.
sentences.zh: 我并不是对树木有什么意见。

sentences.en: I don't have anything against trees.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我非常喜欢树，就像来自佛蒙特州的任何一个热爱户外运动的人一样。

sentences.en: In fact, I love trees, just as much as the next outdoorsy guy from Vermont.
sentences.zh: 但我也报道气候变化够久了，深知世上并没有什么灵丹妙药。

sentences.en: But I've also been reporting on climate change long enough to know that there are no silver bullets.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论植树的方式给人的感觉，你知道的，有点过于简单化了。

sentences.en: And the way people were talking about tree planting felt, you know, a little simplistic.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，气候变化是一个极其复杂的问题，而我们却打算把它浓缩成一句标语。

sentences.en: It was like, here's this enormously complicated issue, climate change, and we're just going to boil it down to a slogan.
sentences.zh: 种树，拯救地球。

sentences.en: Plant trees, save the earth.
sentences.zh: 好吧，每当我听到这句话或这种言论时，我的压力指数就会急剧上升。

sentences.en: Well, whenever I hear that phrase or that discourse, my stress level goes up enormously.
sentences.zh: 这位是理查德·林赛，东伦敦大学可持续发展研究所的科学家。

sentences.en: This is Richard Lindsay, a scientist at the University of East London's Sustainability Research Institute.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在说，让我们种一百万棵树吧。

sentences.en: Everybody is saying, let's plant a million trees.
sentences.zh: 让我们种十亿棵树吧。

sentences.en: Let's plant a billion trees.
sentences.zh: 是的，我完全赞成这一点。

sentences.en: Yes, I'm all in favor of that.
sentences.zh: 但让我们在对的地方种对的树吧。

sentences.en: But let's plant the right tree in the right place.
sentences.zh: 理查德有亲身经历，看到过许多树被种在错误的地方。

sentences.en: And Richard has personal experience watching a lot of trees get planted in the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪80年代，他就亲眼目睹了苏格兰一项有争议的植树计划的影响，

sentences.en: Back in the 1980s, he saw firsthand the impacts of a controversial tree planting scheme in Scotland
sentences.zh: 该计划最终威胁到了世界上最特殊的生态系统之一。

sentences.en: that ended up threatening one of the most special ecosystems in the world.
sentences.zh: 这些树并不是为了对抗气候变化而种的。

sentences.en: The trees weren't being planted to fight climate change.
sentences.zh: 我想把这一点说清楚。

sentences.en: I want to be really clear about that.
sentences.zh: 那时候几乎没有人谈论气候变化。

sentences.en: Very few people were talking about climate change back then.
sentences.zh: 但苏格兰发生的事情依然应该成为我们今天植树造林努力的前车之鉴。

sentences.en: But the story of what happened in Scotland should still serve as a cautionary tale for our tree planting efforts today.
sentences.zh: 因为森林并不是唯一储存碳的生态系统。

sentences.en: Because forests aren't the only ecosystems that store carbon.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们确实在种树时，我们需要非常小心我们在哪里种树，

sentences.en: And so when we do plant trees, we need to be really careful about where we're planting them
sentences.zh: 以及它们种下之后会发生什么。

sentences.en: and what happens after they go in the ground.
sentences.zh: 不列颠群岛过去曾被森林覆盖。

sentences.en: The British Isles used to be covered in forests.
sentences.zh: 但在几个世纪以来将林地转变为农业用地之后，标志性的英国林地已成为历史的大部分。

sentences.en: But after centuries of converting forest land to agriculture, the iconic British woodland was largely a thing of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪，英国由于自身木材不足而不得不进口木材。

sentences.en: By the 20th century, Great Britain was importing wood because it didn't have enough of its own.
sentences.zh: 因此，在20世纪80年代，政府开始利用税收优惠来鼓励私人资助全国各地的植树活动。

sentences.en: And so in the 1980s, the government started using tax breaks to encourage private citizens to fund tree planting efforts around the country.
sentences.zh: 目标是增加英国的木材供应。

sentences.en: The goal was to boost the UK's timber supply.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个很好的税收优惠，特别是对超级富豪而言。

sentences.en: And it was a really good tax break, especially for the super rich.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有这样的人，比如，乐队“创世纪”的会计师让他们参与了进来。

sentences.en: So we had people like, well, the band Genesis, their accountants, got them involved in this.
sentences.zh: 是的，许多知名人士都投资了这个项目，因为他们确信这是一件好事，毕竟种树是件好事，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, a number of sort of high-profile names who all invested in this, having been convinced that it was a good thing because, of course, planting trees is a good thing, is it not?
sentences.zh: 但开始出现一些疑问：这些树究竟要种在哪里？

sentences.en: But questions started to emerge about where exactly these trees were going to go.
sentences.zh: 为了让这个计划行之通，投资者需要大片未开发、无人问津的土地。

sentences.en: In order for this to work, investors needed large tracts of undeveloped, unwanted land.
sentences.zh: 有一个地方完美符合这个标准。

sentences.en: And there was one place that met that criteria perfectly.
sentences.zh: 它被称为流之乡。

sentences.en: It was called the flow country.
sentences.zh: 流之乡是苏格兰远北部一片广阔开阔的地区，看起来几乎像是北极苔原。

sentences.en: The flow country is a vast open area in far north of Scotland that looks almost like the Arctic tundra.
sentences.zh: 苔原（tundra）这个词来自芬 D 语单词 tuntri，意思是树木线之外。

sentences.en: The term tundra comes from the Finnish word tuntri, which means beyond the treeline.
sentences.zh: 这确实向你说明了这里的整体景观。

sentences.en: And so that really tells you something about the overall landscape.
sentences.zh: 它基本上没有树木。

sentences.en: It's essentially treeless.
sentences.zh: 流之乡被称为毯状泥炭沼泽。

sentences.en: The flow country is what's called a blanket bog.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是全欧洲最大的毯状泥炭沼泽。

sentences.en: It's actually the largest blanket bog in all of Europe.
sentences.zh: 欣赏这片景观最好的方式或许是从飞机上俯瞰。

sentences.en: The best way to appreciate the landscape might be in an airplane.
sentences.zh: 从空中看，它就像一块波斯地毯，上面点缀着五颜六色的泥炭藓，并散落着一个个小水洼。

sentences.en: From the sky, it looks like a Persian rug, streaked with colorful sphagnum mosses and dotted with little pools of water.
sentences.zh: 但当你在地面上时，就很难去欣赏它了。

sentences.en: But it's harder to appreciate when you're on the ground.
sentences.zh: 大部分景观将是这种湿润、泥泞、松软、色彩相当丰富的泥炭藓地毯。

sentences.en: The majority of the landscape will be this wet, boggy, soft, really quite colorful carpet of bog mosses.
sentences.zh: 因此，当你走过它时，有点像走在弹簧床垫上，只不过你需要穿胶靴。

sentences.en: So as you walk across it, it's a bit like walking across a sprung mattress, except you need rubber boots.
sentences.zh: 是的，一个湿漉漉的，湿漉漉的床垫。

sentences.en: Yeah, a soggy, a soggy mattress.
sentences.zh: 湿漉漉是一个很好的词，弗雷德。

sentences.en: Soggy is a very good word, Fred.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰有一句俗语，说夏天是一年中最美好的一天。

sentences.en: There's a saying in Scotland that summer is the best day of the year.
sentences.zh: 又冷又潮湿，降雨量巨大。

sentences.en: It's cold and damp and gets an enormous amount of rainfall.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，一切完美。

sentences.en: But otherwise, it's perfect.
sentences.zh: 这真的是我在地球上最喜欢的地方之一。

sentences.en: It truly is one of my favorite places on earth.
sentences.zh: 是的，苏格兰美妙的糟糕天气实际上为一种奇妙物质的形成创造了完美条件。

sentences.en: Yeah, and beautiful Scotland's terrible weather actually creates the perfect conditions for an incredible substance to form.
sentences.zh: 它被称为泥炭，流之乡就是由它组成的。

sentences.en: It's called peat, and it's what the flow country is made of.
sentences.zh: 这里的土地水分饱和度极高，以至于几乎没有氧气，植物残体很难分解。

sentences.en: The land is so saturated that there's very little oxygen, and it's really hard for plant matter to break down.
sentences.zh: 因此，经过成千上万年的时间，这种部分分解的物质（即泥炭）一直在慢慢积累。

sentences.en: And so over thousands and thousands of years, this partially decomposed material, or peat, has been slowly accumulating.
sentences.zh: 在流之乡的某些地方，泥炭现在已经有30多英尺深。

sentences.en: In some parts of the flow country, the peat is now more than 30 feet deep.
sentences.zh: 从气候的角度来看，泥炭神奇的地方在于它储存了大量的碳。

sentences.en: And the amazing thing about peat, from a climate perspective, is that it stores a ton of carbon.
sentences.zh: 我爱上了泥炭地，因为它们是美丽的生态系统，同时也是碳储存的全球主力军。

sentences.en: I fell in love with peatlands because they are these beautiful ecosystems, but they also are global powerhouses for carbon storage.
sentences.zh: 这位是梅里特·图雷茨基，或者如她在推特上所知的那样，被称为泥炭女王。

sentences.en: This is Merit Turetsky, or the Queen of Peat, as she's known on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 她是科罗拉多大学博尔德分校北极和高山研究所所长。

sentences.en: She's the director of the Institute of Arctic and Alpine Research at UC Boulder.
sentences.zh: 她说泥炭地就像地下致密的碳口袋。

sentences.en: And she says that peatlands are like these dense, underground pockets of carbon.
sentences.zh: 因此，每平方米泥炭地中储存的碳量通常比森林或农业环境中同等面积的土地高出10倍、15倍。

sentences.en: So the amount of carbon stored in peatlands on a meter square basis is often 10 times, 15 times higher than that same area of land in a forest or in an agricultural setting.
sentences.zh: 在保护土壤中的碳以及将碳阻隔在大气之外方面，这些绝对是热点地区。

sentences.en: And these are true hotspots when it comes to protecting carbon in soils and keeping that carbon out of the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 事实上，世界各地的泥炭地所含的碳比全世界所有植被加起来还要多。

sentences.en: Peatlands around the world actually contain more carbon than all the world's vegetation combined.
sentences.zh: 但在80年代，大多数人并不了解泥炭这种惊人的力量。

sentences.en: But back in the 80s, most people didn't know about this incredible power of peat.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，那就是沼泽曾被视为令人不快、应该避开的恐怖地方。

sentences.en: If anything, bogs were seen as unpleasant, scary places to be avoided.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是它们里面充满了死人——在无氧软泥中腌制了几个世纪的古代沼泽尸体。

sentences.en: In part because they were filled with dead people, ancient bog bodies that had been pickled for centuries in the anaerobic muck.
sentences.zh: 其中一些尸体似乎是青铜时代和铁器时代的宗教祭品。

sentences.en: Some of these bodies appear to be ritual sacrifices from the Bronze and Iron Ages.
sentences.zh: 一旦这些尸体被扔进沼泽，它们就会得到非常有效的保存。

sentences.en: Once those bodies were tossed into the bog, they became very efficiently preserved.
sentences.zh: 由于保护泥炭免于分解的相同条件，这些沼泽尸体并没有分解。

sentences.en: Because of those same conditions that protect peat from decomposition, the bog bodies didn't decompose.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，这些保存得诡异完好的尸体会从北欧的沼泽中浮出水面。

sentences.en: And occasionally, these eerily well-preserved corpses would surface from the bogs of Northern Europe.
sentences.zh: 不用说，在苏格兰，阴森森、湿漉漉的泥炭地绝对算不上什么受欢迎的地方。

sentences.en: Needless to say, in Scotland, the spooky, soggy peatland wasn't exactly a popular spot.
sentences.zh: 流之乡在当地有一个缩写代号，叫做曼巴。

sentences.en: The flow country was known locally by an acronym, Mamba.
sentences.zh: 它闻名遐迩地被称为曼巴之乡。

sentences.en: Famously, it was called Mamba Country.
sentences.zh: 方圆数英里什么也没有。

sentences.en: Miles and miles of bugger all.
sentences.zh: 因此，在20世纪80年代，当林业行业开始寻找大片未开发的土地来种树时，

sentences.en: And so, in the 1980s, when the forest industry started looking for large tracts of undeveloped land to plant trees,
sentences.zh: 流之乡是一个显而易见的选择。

sentences.en: the flow country was an obvious choice.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它被视为一片荒地。

sentences.en: You know, it was seen as a wasteland.
sentences.zh: 所以当地人被林业行业说服，相信这将为该地区带来一种新的经济。

sentences.en: So the local people had been convinced by the forest industry that this was going to bring a new economy to the area.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当地人当然感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: So, you know, of course, local people were really excited.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情有点像是一场赛跑：一方是林业集团，他们开始排干泥炭沼泽并种植树木；

sentences.en: What happened next was kind of a race between the forestry groups, who started draining the peat bogs and planting trees,
sentences.zh: 另一方是自然保护集团，他们开始试图在这片脆弱的景观被彻底覆盖之前，对其中的所有生物多样性进行编目。

sentences.en: and conservation groups, who began trying to catalog all the biodiversity in this fragile landscape before it was completely covered up.
sentences.zh: 这就是我真正被卷入整个流之乡故事的地方，

sentences.en: And that's where I was really sucked into the whole flow country story,
sentences.zh: 因为我基本上被指派负责一项调查项目，以确定流之乡是否包含任何重要的东西，

sentences.en: because essentially I was tasked with running a survey program to establish whether the flow country contained anything of importance,
sentences.zh: 任何我们应该担心失去的东西。

sentences.en: anything that we should be concerned about losing.
sentences.zh: 理查德组建了一个科学家团队。

sentences.en: Richard assembled a team of scientists.
sentences.zh: 他们打包了帐篷和露营装备、相机和食物，坐着从伦敦出发的火车，

sentences.en: They packed up tents and camping gear, cameras and food, and took the train from London,
sentences.zh: 向北行驶400多英里，直抵苏格兰的最尖端。

sentences.en: over 400 miles north to the tippy top of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 理查德立刻就被这个地方迷住了。

sentences.en: And right away, Richard was taken with the place.
sentences.zh: 这里太非同寻常了。

sentences.en: It was extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 首先是这里的寂静。

sentences.en: First of all, in the silence.
sentences.zh: 但很快，他也熟悉了这个地方的声音和气味。

sentences.en: But pretty quickly, he got acquainted with the sounds and smells of the place, too.
sentences.zh: 连续几个星期，他和他的团队在这个湿软的床垫上四处跋涉，

sentences.en: For weeks, he and his team would tramp around on top of the soggy mattress,
sentences.zh: 记录沼泽中的所有野生动植物。

sentences.en: documenting all of the wildlife in the bog.
sentences.zh: 食肉植物、蜻蜓、水甲虫、潜鸟和金鸻。

sentences.en: Carnivorous plants, dragonflies, water beetles, loons, and golden plovers.
sentences.zh: 过程很艰难，但除了湿漉漉的袜子，理查德对这些漫长的徒步旅行怀有美好的回忆。

sentences.en: It was tough going, but apart from the wet socks, Richard remembers these long walks fondly.
sentences.zh: 因为你走在上面会轻轻地弹起，脚下有一种软绵绵、黏糊糊的感觉，

sentences.en: Because you sort of bounce gently along, there's a sort of squish, squish on the foot,
sentences.zh: 这是一种很好的体验。

sentences.en: and there's the lovely scent of all the heathers and the various sort of flowering plants that wafted up around you.
sentences.zh: 四周飘荡着各种石楠花和开花植物的迷人芬芳。

sentences.en: And in the end, Richard and his team determined that the flow country wasn't a wasteland at all,
sentences.zh: 最终，理查德和他的团队认定，泥炭荒原根本不是什么不毛之地，

sentences.en: but a thriving wetland habitat that had been underappreciated for centuries.
sentences.zh: 而是一个几个世纪以来一直被严重低估的繁荣湿地生态系统。

sentences.en: Essentially, we found that the range of ecosystem types was like nothing,
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，我们发现这里的生态系统类型丰富多样，可以说是……

sentences.en: well, really, that had been described anywhere else in the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，真的可以说是世界上其他任何地方都未曾描述过的。

sentences.en: But as all this was happening, the tree planting was already underway.
sentences.zh: 但就在这一切发生的同时，植树造林工作已经在进行中了。

sentences.en: And so at the same time Richard was discovering the secrets of this delicate landscape,
sentences.zh: 因此，就在理查德探索这片脆弱景观的奥秘的同时，

sentences.en: the forestry companies were tearing it up.
sentences.zh: 林业公司却在将其毁坏。

sentences.en: They plowed up the bogs, drained out all that water,
sentences.zh: 他们犁开泥炭地，排干了所有的积水，

sentences.en: and planted non-native, quick-growing conifers.
sentences.zh: 并种上了外来的、生长迅速的针叶树。

sentences.en: Pretty soon, little patches of evergreen forest were sprouting up all across the flow country.
sentences.zh: 很快，一块块常青林开始在整个泥炭荒原上冒出来。

sentences.en: Although Richard says forest isn't really the right word.
sentences.zh: 尽管理查德说“森林”这个词其实并不贴切。

sentences.en: No, they're plantations.
sentences.zh: 不，它们是人工林。

sentences.en: Plantations established with agricultural densities in mind.
sentences.zh: 按照农业种植密度建立的人工林。

sentences.en: Rows and rows of Sitka spruce and lodgepole pine packed tightly together.
sentences.zh: 一排排的锡特卡云杉和扭叶松紧密地挤在一起。

sentences.en: And these dense plantations were terrible places for native wildlife.
sentences.zh: 这些密集的人工林对本土野生动物来说是个可怕的地方。

sentences.en: They quickly filled up with predators that scared off many of the birds
sentences.zh: 它们很快充斥着捕食者，吓跑了许多鸟类，

sentences.en: that Richard and his team were just beginning to learn about.
sentences.zh: 而理查德和他的团队对这些鸟类才刚刚开始有所了解。

sentences.en: The peatlands were turning into a tree farm.
sentences.zh: 泥炭地正在变成一个树木农场。

sentences.en: So, yeah, pretty soul-destroying.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这相当令人心碎。

sentences.en: As they did their work, Richard and the other scientists were called to testify
sentences.zh: 在开展工作的同时，理查德和其他科学家被召集出席

sentences.en: in local meetings about the forestry project.
sentences.zh: 关于林业项目的当地会议并作证。

sentences.en: And they had to argue that this seemingly empty, worthless landscape was actually worth protecting.
sentences.zh: 他们不得不辩称，这片看似空旷、毫无价值的风景其实非常值得保护。

sentences.en: And essentially, it's our equivalent of the tropical rainforeSt.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，这就是我们这里的热带雨林。

sentences.en: But the forest industry didn't see it that way.
sentences.zh: 但林业行业并不这么认为。

sentences.en: I just have this general memory of being shouted at a lot for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 我只记得一种普遍的记忆，那就是在很长一段时间里被劈头盖脸地大声指责。

sentences.en: They were banging the table and they were shouting at us
sentences.zh: 他们拍着桌子冲我们大喊大叫，

sentences.en: and demanding to know what we thought we were doing.
sentences.zh: 质问我们到底自以为什么在做。

sentences.en: To which our response was, well, we think we're doing our job.
sentences.zh: 对此，我们的回应是，嗯，我们觉得我们在做自己的工作。

sentences.en: You know, our job was to identify important areas of the nation's wildlife heritage.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们的工作就是识别国家野生动物遗产中的重要区域。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what we were doing.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们在做的事情。

sentences.en: Was it weird at the time to be arguing that trees were an environmental problem?
sentences.zh: 当时争论树木是环境问题，这会不会很奇怪？

sentences.en: Oh, that was so difficult, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太艰难了，是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, it's like everything.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这就像任何事情一样。

sentences.en: You know, a medication is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，药物是个好东西。

sentences.en: When used in the right way, in the right place.
sentences.zh: 只要在正确的时间、在正确的地方使用。

sentences.en: Used in the wrong way, in the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 如果在错误的时间、错误的地方使用，

sentences.en: It's a poison.
sentences.zh: 它就是毒药。

sentences.en: And that was the tricky message that we had to try and get across.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们竭力想要传达的那个棘手的信息。

sentences.en: But over time, public opinion began to turn against the tree planting.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，公众舆论开始转向反对植树造林。

sentences.en: A lot of that had to do with the fact that it seemed like an egregious form of tax avoidance.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是因为这看起来像是一种极其严重的避税行为。

sentences.en: But the message about the peatlands was also starting to get through.
sentences.zh: 不过，关于泥炭地的信息也开始逐渐深入人心。

sentences.en: The government eventually agreed to protect about half of the peatland that Richard and his team had surveyed.
sentences.zh: 政府最终同意保护理查德及其团队调查过的大约一半泥炭地。

sentences.en: And then, a couple months later, they completely ended the tax scheme.
sentences.zh: 然后，几个月后，他们彻底终止了这个税收计划。

sentences.en: A colleague phoned me.
sentences.zh: 一位同事给我打了个电话。

sentences.en: He just said, it's gone.
sentences.zh: 他直接说，没了。

sentences.en: I said, what's gone?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么没了？

sentences.en: The forestry ground scheme.
sentences.zh: 林业资助计划。

sentences.en: It's gone.
sentences.zh: 没了。

sentences.en: I remember I had to sit down.
sentences.zh: 我记得我不得不坐下来。

sentences.en: I was so surprised.
sentences.zh: 我太惊讶了。

sentences.en: It was a big win for the bog.
sentences.zh: 这对泥炭地来说是一次重大的胜利。

sentences.en: And the conservationists fighting to protect it.
sentences.zh: 也是为保护它而战的环保主义者们的胜利。

sentences.en: And in the decades that followed, the way people saw the flow country really started to shift.
sentences.zh: 在随后的几十年里，人们对泥炭荒原的看法开始真正发生转变。

sentences.en: It went from being a place people avoided to a place that people wanted to see.
sentences.zh: 它从一个人们避之不及的地方变成了人们渴望一睹芳容的地方。

sentences.en: The largest blanket bog in all of Europe.
sentences.zh: 整个欧洲最大的毯状泥炭地。

sentences.en: And people were coming to visit it, to see this amazing landscape.
sentences.zh: 人们纷纷前来参观，来看这片神奇的风景。

sentences.en: And all of this gradually chipped away at the idea of this is useless wasteland.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切逐渐打破了“这是无用荒地”的想法。

sentences.en: And people began to relate to it as their landscape, their precious landscape.
sentences.zh: 人们开始把它当作自己的风景，自己珍贵的风景来建立情感联系。

sentences.en: But a lot of damage had been done.
sentences.zh: 但破坏已经造成了。

sentences.en: Over 150,000 acres of the flow country had been drained and planted with trees.
sentences.zh: 泥炭荒原有超过 15 万英亩的土地被排干并种上了树。

sentences.en: These trees never really grew very well.
sentences.zh: 这些树其实从来没有长得很好。

sentences.en: They were short and stubby and not very useful as timber.
sentences.zh: 它们又矮又粗壮，作为木材并没有多大用处。

sentences.en: But the plantations pushed out native wildlife that depended on the bog and damaged the precious peat that was storing all that carbon.
sentences.zh: 但人工林排挤了依赖泥炭地生存的本土野生动物，并破坏了储存所有这些碳的珍贵泥炭。

sentences.en: And the flow country wasn't the only place where this kind of thing happened.
sentences.zh: 泥炭荒原并不是唯一发生这种事情的地方。

sentences.en: Chile, to take one example, started incentivizing tree planting around the same time as the UK.
sentences.zh: 以智利为例，它在英国前后也开始推行植树激励政策。

sentences.en: And while they did plant a lot of trees, the effort led to a decline in biodiversity and negligible climate benefits.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们确实种了很多树，但这番努力却导致了生物多样性的下降，气候效益也微乎其微。

sentences.en: In Alberta, Canada, they drained large swaths of bog in order to plant trees, again, starting in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大艾伯塔省，同样从 20 世纪 80 年代开始，他们排干了大片泥炭地用来种树。

sentences.en: But most of those trees burned down in the Fort McMurray Fire of 2016, in part because the once wet ground had been drained dry.
sentences.zh: 但其中绝大多数树木在 2016 年麦克默里堡大火中被烧毁，部分原因正是曾经湿润的土地被排干变干了。

sentences.en: Back in the 1980s, Richard Lindsay and his colleagues were only concerned about the biodiversity and the underappreciated peat bog.
sentences.zh: 早在 20 世纪 80 年代，理查德·林赛和他的同事们仅仅关注生物多样性和那些未被充分重视的泥炭地。

sentences.en: But in recent years, as the urgency of the climate crisis grows, there's been an increased focus on carbon storage in ecosysteMs.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，随着气候危机日益紧迫，人们越来越关注生态系统中的碳储存。

sentences.en: Scientists are studying the carbon dynamics in kelp forests and seagrass beds, and peatlands in particular have been getting a lot of attention for their carbon-storing powers.
sentences.zh: 科学家们正在研究海藻林和海草床中的碳动态，尤其是泥炭地因其强大的固碳能力而备受关注。

sentences.en: You know you've gone mainstream when Alec Baldwin is talking about you in a PSA for the UN.
sentences.zh: 当亚历克·鲍德温在联合国公益广告中谈论你时，你就知道你已经成为主流了。

sentences.en: Peatlands are crucial to fight climate change.
sentences.zh: 泥炭地对应对气候变化至关重要。

sentences.en: And here's the thing about peatlands.
sentences.zh: 关于泥炭地，事实是这样的。

sentences.en: They matter for the planet because they actually store twice as much carbon as all the world's forests together, while covering less than 3% of the land's surface.
sentences.zh: 它们对地球至关重要，因为它们储存的碳实际上是全球所有森林总和的两倍，而其陆地表面积却不到 3%。

sentences.en: So peatlands are the most efficient terrestrial carbon sink on the planet.
sentences.zh: 因此，泥炭地是地球上最高效的陆地碳汇。

sentences.en: This is Roxanne Anderson.
sentences.zh: 这位是罗克珊·安德森。

sentences.en: She's been studying peatlands for a while now at the Environmental Research Institute in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 她目前在苏格兰环境研究所研究泥炭地已经有一段时间了。

sentences.en: And for decades, it felt like she was laboring away in some obscure corner of academia.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，她感觉自己就像是在学术界的某个不知名角落里默默耕耘。

sentences.en: She didn't have journalists like me bugging her for interviews.
sentences.zh: 她没有像我这样的记者围着她死缠烂打地要求采访。

sentences.en: But that's changing.
sentences.zh: 但情况正在改变。

sentences.en: I think this year alone, I must have given something like 15 or 20 interviews.
sentences.zh: 我想仅今年一年，我就接受了大约 15 或 20 次采访。

sentences.en: But Anderson says that when it comes to carbon storage, peatlands still don't get the attention that forests do.
sentences.zh: 不过安德森表示，在固碳方面，泥炭地受到的关注仍然不如森林。

sentences.en: She thinks it's because all the carbon in a peatland is below ground.
sentences.zh: 她认为这是因为泥炭地里的所有碳都在地下。

sentences.en: I think that it's because it's not visible.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为它肉眼看不见。

sentences.en: That's why the name of your podcast really resonated.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你们播客的名字能引起强烈共鸣的原因。

sentences.en: If you look at a forest, you see the trees, you see the vegetation, you see where the carbon is, you see why it's taking up carbon.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一片森林，你能看到树木，看到植被，看到碳在哪里，看到它为什么在吸收碳。

sentences.en: But even though the carbon in a peatland is hidden underground, it's not locked away forever.
sentences.zh: 尽管泥炭地中的碳隐藏在地下，但它并非被永远锁住。

sentences.en: Just as a forest can burn down, a peatland can be degraded, can be gobbled up for agriculture or ranching.
sentences.zh: 正如森林可能会被烧毁一样，泥炭地也可能会退化，可能会被侵占用于农业或牧业。

sentences.en: And when that happens, a lot of its carbon goes up into the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，其大部分碳就会释放到大气中。

sentences.en: And the carbon sink becomes a carbon source.
sentences.zh: 碳汇就变成了碳源。

sentences.en: And that's what happened in the flow country.
sentences.zh: 泥炭荒原发生的就是这种情况。

sentences.en: Except, in this case, the crop that was gobbling up the peatland was trees.
sentences.zh: 只不过，这一次吞噬泥炭地的“农作物”是树木。

sentences.en: When you drain a peat bog to plant trees, it releases carbon.
sentences.zh: 当你排干泥炭地的水来种树时，它就会释放碳。

sentences.en: And then, as the trees grow, their roots impact the way the carbon in the soil is processed.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着树木生长，它们的根系会影响土壤中碳的处理方式。

sentences.en: And the carbon losses from the soil can actually exceed the amount of carbon that's taken up in the tree.
sentences.zh: 土壤中碳的流失实际上可能超过树木吸收的碳量。

sentences.en: So planting trees on peat, on deep peat particularly, is really, really not a good idea.
sentences.zh: 因此，在泥炭上植树，尤其是深厚泥炭地上，真的、真的不是一个好主意。

sentences.en: It leads to unintended consequences of basically losing more carbon than you can gain through the trees.
sentences.zh: 它会导致意想不到的后果，即释放的碳基本上多于树木所能吸收的碳。

sentences.en: And so now, in the flow country, the best thing for the climate may actually be to cut trees down.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，在泥炭荒原，对气候最好的做法可能实际上是把树木砍掉。

sentences.en: It's quite claustrophobic being in some of these dark, damp plantations.
sentences.zh: 置身于这些阴暗潮湿的人工林中，会有一种相当幽闭恐惧的感觉。

sentences.en: And so when you start taking them down and start opening up the landscape again,
sentences.zh: 因此，当你开始砍伐它们并重新开辟这片景观时，

sentences.en: in some ways it's actually quite cathartic.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上讲，这其实是一种相当宣泄的体验。

sentences.en: This is Paul Turner, a warden with the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds.
sentences.zh: 这位是保罗·特纳，皇家鸟类保护协会的一名管理员。

sentences.en: And in 1995, the RSPB purchased a 50,000-acre reserve in the flow country,
sentences.zh: 1995 年，英国皇家鸟类保护协会在泥炭荒原购买了一块占地 5 万英亩的保护区，

sentences.en: on land that had been heavily planted with trees.
sentences.zh: 这片土地曾经被大量种植树木。

sentences.en: Since then, they've been working to restore the bog.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，他们一直致力于恢复泥炭地。

sentences.en: We've really spent 25 years trying to repair damage that was done in the 70s and 80s to bits of the peatlands.
sentences.zh: 我们确实花了 25 年的时间来试图修复 70 和 80 年代对部分泥炭地造成的破坏。

sentences.en: Some of the contractors doing this repair work are actually the same local people who drained the bog back in the 80s.
sentences.zh: 参与这项修复工作的有些承包商，实际上就是当年在 80 年代排干泥炭地的当地人。

sentences.en: First, they cut the trees down and haul them out.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们把树木砍倒并运出去。

sentences.en: Then, the crucial next step is to re-wet the soil.
sentences.zh: 然后，至关重要的下一步是让土壤重新湿润。

sentences.en: They build dams in the peat to try to return the water table to its normal level and get that soggy bog back.
sentences.zh: 他们在泥炭中筑坝，试图将地下水位恢复到正常水平，让那片湿漉漉的泥炭地恢复原貌。

sentences.en: A lot of this work is done with heavy machinery, and it does not look pretty.
sentences.zh: 这项工作很大程度上是由重型机械完成的，看起来确实不太美观。

sentences.en: And yeah, you have days where you think, actually, this is quite a destructive process.
sentences.zh: 是的，有时候你会觉得，其实这是一个相当具有破坏性的过程。

sentences.en: But when you start seeing some of the work that we did 10, 15 years ago,
sentences.zh: 但当你看到我们 10 年、15 年前做的一些工作时，

sentences.en: it really makes you feel quite good about what you're trying to achieve with it.
sentences.zh: 真的会让你对你试图通过它实现的目标感到非常欣慰。

sentences.en: Roxanne Anderson has studied the bogs that Paul Turner and the RSPB have restored to try and understand the climate impacts.
sentences.zh: 罗克珊·安德森研究了保罗·特纳和皇家鸟类保护协会恢复的泥炭地，试图了解其对气候的影响。

sentences.en: What we've found is that when you take trees down from a peatland and do the restoration,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当你从泥炭地上砍伐树木并进行恢复时，

sentences.en: initially, it releases carbon.
sentences.zh: 最初它会释放碳。

sentences.en: That's not very surprising because of the kind of physical damage that you have to do in terms of cutting the woods and everything else.
sentences.zh: 这并不奇怪，因为砍伐树木以及其他方面必须进行某种物理破坏。

sentences.en: But over the course of decades of restoration, the bogs have switched back from a carbon source to a carbon sink.
sentences.zh: 但经过几十年的恢复，泥炭地又从碳源转回了碳汇。

sentences.en: So effectively returning this kind of carbon benefits or climate benefits of peatlands.
sentences.zh: 从而有效地恢复了泥炭地的这种碳效益或气候效益。

sentences.en: But as they do this work, Paul Turner keeps running into the same problem that Richard Lindsay did 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但在开展这项工作的同时，保罗·特纳不断遇到 30 年前理查德·林赛遇到过的问题。

sentences.en: It's hard to explain to people why trees, in this very specific situation, are bad for the ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 很难向人们解释为什么在这种非常特定的情况下，树木对生态系统是有害的。

sentences.en: There are a lot of people that don't really understand why we're cutting trees down.
sentences.zh: 有很多人并不真正理解我们为什么要砍树。

sentences.en: It's because surely planting trees is the best thing to do.
sentences.zh: 因为大家觉得植树肯定是最好的做法。

sentences.en: And as I mentioned before, planting trees in the right place is definitely a really good thing to do.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，在正确的地方植树绝对是一件非常好的事。

sentences.en: Paul is not anti-tree.
sentences.zh: 保罗并不是反对树木。

sentences.en: In fact, the RSPB actually helps manage another piece of land in Scotland, in the Cairngorn Mountains,
sentences.zh: 事实上，英国皇家鸟类保护协会还在苏格兰凯恩戈姆山脉管理着另一块土地，

sentences.en: where they are actively planting trees in an effort to restore the forest and sequester carbon.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里积极植树，以恢复森林并封存碳。

sentences.en: And the Scottish government is helping fund both of these efforts.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰政府正在资助这两项工作。

sentences.en: Scotland has a goal of restoring over 600,000 acres of peat bog by 2030.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰的目标是在 2030 年前恢复超过 60 万英亩的泥炭地。

sentences.en: And at the same time, they want to plant 30,000 acres of new forest each year.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们希望每年种植 3 万英亩的新森林。

sentences.en: They are planting trees in one place, just as they are cutting trees down in another.
sentences.zh: 他们在一个地方种树，就像在另一个地方砍树一样。

sentences.en: It's understanding that not all habitats are equal, that not all habitats should have trees on them.
sentences.zh: 这是在理解并非所有栖息地都是一样的，并非所有栖息地都应该长满树木。

sentences.en: And that when we're talking about climate change mitigation, that one answer doesn't apply to every problem.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论缓解气候变化时，不能用一个答案去套用所有问题。

sentences.en: Forests are great, but they aren't great everywhere.
sentences.zh: 森林很好，但并不意味着到处都好。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I love forests.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我很喜欢森林。

sentences.en: But I love other ecosystems too.
sentences.zh: 但我也喜欢其他生态系统。

sentences.en: This is a forest scientist named Forrest, Forrest Fleischman.
sentences.zh: 这位森林科学家名叫福雷斯特，福雷斯特·弗莱施曼。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I mean, one of the big mistakes that the Trillian Tree paper made is they sort of said,
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，那篇关于万棵树的论文所犯的一个重大错误是，他们某种程度上说，

sentences.en: well, areas without trees don't have carbon.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有树的地区没有碳。

sentences.en: And that's not true, because areas without trees have carbon below ground.
sentences.zh: 这是不对的，因为没有树的地区地下也有碳。

sentences.en: And not just peatlands.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是泥炭地。

sentences.en: Healthy grasslands also store carbon underground.
sentences.zh: 健康的草原也会在地下储存碳。

sentences.en: So instead of just thinking about how many trees we can plant,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们不应只考虑我们可以种植多少棵树，

sentences.en: we should be thinking about all the different ways we can maximize carbon storage in any given landscape without sacrificing biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 而应该考虑所有不同的方法，以便在不牺牲生物多样性的前提下，最大限度地提高任何特定景观中的碳储存。

sentences.en: That might mean restoring peatlands or protecting healthy grasslands and forests.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着恢复泥炭地，或者保护健康的草原和森林。

sentences.en: And it might mean planting more trees.
sentences.zh: 这也可能意味着种植更多的树木。

sentences.en: And if planting trees is the right thing for a landscape, we're going to have to do more than just plant them.
sentences.zh: 如果种树对一片景观来说是正确的做法，我们就必须付出比仅仅种树更多的努力。

sentences.en: Forrest Fleischman has studied tree planting efforts that are being done for climate change.
sentences.zh: 福雷斯特·弗莱施曼研究了为应对气候变化而开展的植树造林工作。

sentences.en: And he's found that often they fail because all of the focus is on that initial act of getting the saplings in the ground.
sentences.zh: 他发现这些努力往往以失败告终，因为所有的焦点都集中在最初把树苗种进土里的那个行动上。

sentences.en: Because it's something that a politician can walk in and do and get a picture taken and be on the front page of the newspaper or be on the TV.
sentences.zh: 因为这是政客可以亲自去干、拍张照片、登上报纸头条或上电视的事情。

sentences.en: But then often in the years that follow, those trees get cut down by people or eaten by cows or burned in a fire.
sentences.zh: 但随后的几年里，这些树木往往会被人砍伐、被牛吃掉或在火灾中烧毁。

sentences.en: So this dialogue, it says, oh, we need to plant a trillion trees.
sentences.zh: 所以这种对话说，哦，我们需要种植一万亿棵树。

sentences.en: Well, actually, we don't need to plant a trillion trees.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实上，我们不需要种植一万亿棵树。

sentences.en: Let's say the trillion trees is right.
sentences.zh: 假设种植一万亿棵树是正确的。

sentences.en: We need to make sure that a trillion trees grow.
sentences.zh: 我们需要确保的是一万亿棵树能够长大成材。

sentences.en: And making sure that trees grow is more complicated than planting them.
sentences.zh: 而确保树木长大比种植它们要复杂得多。

sentences.en: Fleischman says the first step is to stop cutting down the healthy forests that we have left.
sentences.zh: 弗莱施曼说，第一步是停止砍伐我们仅存的健康森林。

sentences.en: We need to stop illegal logging and boycott the companies that are driving deforestation.
sentences.zh: 我们需要制止非法采伐，并抵制那些驱动森林砍伐的公司。

sentences.en: And work to protect the rights of indigenous people who are often the best protectors of forests.
sentences.zh: 还要努力保护原住民的权利，他们往往是森林最好的守护者。

sentences.en: And where we do plant new forests, we need to work with local people to make sure that they benefit from the new trees and are invested in keeping them growing.
sentences.zh: 在我们确实种植新森林的地方，我们需要与当地人民合作，确保他们从新树木中受益，并投入到让树木持续生长的行动中。

sentences.en: So when we start thinking about it this way, it really becomes a political and economic problem, not a technical tree planting problem.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们开始从这个角度思考时，它实际上成了一个政治和经济问题，而不是一个技术性的植树问题。

sentences.en: I think that people get really excited about tree planting in part because it's a solution that seems to exist outside of politics and economics.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对植树感到非常兴奋，部分原因在于这是一个似乎独立于政治和经济之外的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's this simple, natural solution that doesn't require us to pass massive legislation or build a whole new energy system.
sentences.zh: 这是一个简单、自然的解决方案，不需要我们通过大规模的立法或建立全新的能源系统。

sentences.en: But the truth is that climate change is fundamentally a complicated political and economic and technological problem.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，气候变化从根本上说是一个复杂的政治、经济和技术问题。

sentences.en: There is no one perfect solution.
sentences.zh: 没有单一的完美解决方案。

sentences.en: But we need to solve it anyway.
sentences.zh: 但我们无论如何都需要解决它。

sentences.en: Bogs are the beSt.
sentences.zh: 沼泽最棒了。

sentences.en: We have so many more cool facts about bogs after this.
sentences.zh: 接下来的节目中，我们还有更多关于沼泽的超酷冷知识。

sentences.en: So Emmett is back and we're going to talk about bogs.
sentences.zh: 所以埃默特回来了，我们要来聊聊沼泽。

sentences.en: Yeah, so one of the things that I found interesting in learning all about bogs was all the language around them.
sentences.zh: 是的，在了解所有关于沼泽的知识时，我发现有趣的事情之一就是与之相关的所有语言。

sentences.en: You know, you've got so many different words for bogs.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你有那么多不同的词汇来形容沼泽。

sentences.en: Bog, fen, mire, moor, marsh, swamp, puckusin.
sentences.zh: 泥炭藓沼、高位泥炭沼、低位泥炭沼、沼泽、泽地、水苔沼。

sentences.en: This is Merit Terecki again, the queen of peat from our story.
sentences.zh: 这位又是玛丽特·特雷茨基，我们故事里的泥炭女王。

sentences.en: And she says that, you know, these aren't synonyms necessarily.
sentences.zh: 她说，你知道，这些不一定完全是同义词。

sentences.en: There are subtle differences between all these different words.
sentences.zh: 所有这些不同的词汇之间存在着微妙的区别。

sentences.en: Some of them are rooted in ecology and wetland classification.
sentences.zh: 其中一些植根于生态学和湿地分类。

sentences.en: Some of them are regional.
sentences.zh: 其中一些具有地方特色。

sentences.en: But there's also this whole sort of metaphorical side to bog language, wetland language.
sentences.zh: 但沼泽语言、湿地语言也存在着一种完全隐喻的层面。

sentences.en: Like we use a lot of these words a lot, actually, not in a peatland science way, but in this kind of more poetic metaphorical sense.
sentences.zh: 就像我们实际上经常使用这些词中的很多个，不是以泥炭地科学的方式，而是以这种更具诗意、隐喻的意义。

sentences.en: And usually bog language connotes stuckness.
sentences.zh: 通常沼泽语言暗指陷入困境。

sentences.en: Right, like getting bogged down in something.
sentences.zh: 没错，就像陷入某事无法自拔一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: But there's a lot of other examples, like a quagmire is a type of bog.
sentences.zh: 但还有很多其他的例子，比如沼泽地（quagmire）就是一种沼泽。

sentences.en: And you can get mired in something.
sentences.zh: 你可能会陷入（mired）某种困境。

sentences.en: A mire is a type of bog.
sentences.zh: 泥沼（mire）是一种沼泽。

sentences.en: Or actually, I think a bog is a type of mire.
sentences.zh: 或者实际上，我认为沼泽（bog）是泥沼的一种。

sentences.en: It's like a square rectangle situation.
sentences.zh: 这就像正方形和长方形的关系。

sentences.en: A morass is another word for kind of marshy, boggy wetland, but also like a confusing situation that you might get stuck in.
sentences.zh: Morass是另一种用来形容有点像沼泽、泥泞的湿地的词，但也用来比喻你可能会陷入的混乱局势。

sentences.en: So what is the explanation for why we use these words so much when most people probably don't experience bogs on a really regular basis?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么大多数人可能并不经常接触沼泽，我们却如此频繁地使用这些词，这该如何解释呢？

sentences.en: You know, I think that for Merit Tretzky, she says that it's like even though bogs are these places that we don't necessarily spend a lot of time,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为对于玛丽特·特雷茨基来说，她说这就好比尽管沼泽是我们不一定会花很多时间去的地方，

sentences.en: humans have always been fascinated by them.
sentences.zh: 人类一直对它们着迷。

sentences.en: And they've always represented this like almost supernatural in-between space.
sentences.zh: 它们一直代表着这种几乎超自然的中间地带。

sentences.en: And I think because of the mysteriousness of that, not being land, not being water, not being fully alive, not being fully dead, they are really fascinating to us.
sentences.zh: 我想正是因为这种神秘感——既不是陆地，也不是水域，不是完全活着，也不是完全死去——它们对我们有着极大的吸引力。

sentences.en: And so bogs in movies, in pop culture, in literature, often represent a place where people can hide from society or where you can potentially get loSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，电影、流行文化和文学中的沼泽，通常代表着人们可以躲避社会，或者可能迷路的地方。

sentences.en: And this is totally true in books and movies.
sentences.zh: 这在书籍和电影中完全是真的。

sentences.en: Like I remember in Wuthering Heights, you know, you have the moors, which are often are presented throughout the book as this kind of foreboding landscape where they might,
sentences.zh: 就像我记得在《呼啸山庄》里，你知道的，有荒原，在整本书中，它们经常被呈现为一种充满不祥预感的风景，在那里他们可能会，

sentences.en: you know, Catherine Heathcliff might get lost or drown.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，凯瑟琳或希刺克厉夫可能会迷路或溺水。

sentences.en: Or in Lord of the Rings, they sort of wind their way through these marshes that are filled with dead faces looking up at them.
sentences.zh: 或者在《指环王》中，他们穿行于这些沼泽之中，里面到处都是死者的面孔，向上注视着他们。

sentences.en: There are dead things, dead faces in the water.
sentences.zh: 水里有死物，有死去的面孔。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, the one that really got me was the swamp of sadness and the never-ending story, you know, where his horse actually gets swallowed up in it.
sentences.zh: 当我还是个孩子的时候，真正震撼我的是《大荒芜的故事》中的悲伤沼泽，你知道的，他的马真的被它吞噬了。

sentences.en: It's just so tragic.
sentences.zh: 真是太悲惨了。

sentences.en: It's so upsetting.
sentences.zh: 太让人难过了。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全是这样。

sentences.en: I almost pulled a clip from that, but it was like too kind of unpleasant to listen to this little boy screaming about his drowning horse.
sentences.zh: 我差点从里面截取一段音频，但听一个小男孩为他溺水的马尖叫，实在有点太让人难受了。

sentences.en: It's very sad.
sentences.zh: 非常悲伤。

sentences.en: You know, the one that really comes to mind for me is the princess bride.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我脑海中浮现的真正例子是《公主新娘》。

sentences.en: You know, the characters are traversing or navigating their way through a fire swamp where, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，角色们正在穿行或摸索着穿过火之沼泽，在那里，你知道的，

sentences.en: bursts of flames come up through the soil and they have to dodge these hazards.
sentences.zh: 阵阵烈焰从土壤中窜出，他们必须躲避这些危险。

sentences.en: I mean, what are the three terrors of the fire swamp?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，火之沼泽的三大恐怖是什么？

sentences.en: One, the flame spurt.
sentences.zh: 第一，喷火口。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: There's a popping sand proceeding each.
sentences.zh: 每个喷火前都会伴随爆裂沙响。

sentences.en: We can avoid that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以避开那个。

sentences.en: Two, the lightning sand.
sentences.zh: 第二，闪电沙。

sentences.en: But you were clever enough to discover what that looks like, so in the future we can avoid that too.
sentences.zh: 但你很聪明，发现了它长什么样，所以将来我们也可以避开它。

sentences.en: Wesley, what about the RUSs?
sentences.zh: 韦斯利，那巨型啮齿动物呢？

sentences.en: Rodents of unusual size?
sentences.zh: 不寻常体型的啮齿动物？

sentences.en: I don't think they exiSt.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它们存在。

sentences.en: Yeah, how could you forget the rodents of unusual size?
sentences.zh: 是啊，你怎么能忘记那些巨型啮齿动物呢？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, you know, the RUSs obviously don't really exist, but Teresky says that some aspects of the fire swamp, like, aren't quite as far-fetched as you might imagine.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，巨型啮齿动物显然并不是真的存在，但特雷茨基说，火之沼泽的某些方面，比如，并不像你想象的那么异想天开。

sentences.en: There are gases, some of them are flammable, that are produced in these very wet, saturated bog systeMs.
sentences.zh: 在这些非常潮湿、饱和的沼泽系统中会产生气体，其中一些是易燃的。

sentences.en: We don't often see flames leaping up through a bog system, but there is a lot of methane produced because of, you know, this really anaerobic decomposition.
sentences.zh: 我们不常看到火焰在沼泽系统中窜起，但由于，你知道的，这种真正无氧的分解，确实会产生大量的甲烷。

sentences.en: And that methane actually could be flammable.
sentences.zh: 而这些甲烷实际上可能是易燃的。

sentences.en: I mean, that is shocking that that could be based in any kind of reality.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太令人震惊了，它竟然可以有任何形式的现实依据。

sentences.en: I mean, come to think of it, you know, the dead people in the bogs, like the Lord of the Rings, that also feels like a reference to the bog people that we, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仔细想想，你知道，沼泽里的死人，就像《指环王》里那样，这也感觉像是在致敬我们在本集主体部分中，你知道，

sentences.en: touch on in the main body of the episode.
sentences.zh: 略有涉及的沼泽人。

sentences.en: Right, bog bodies.
sentences.zh: 没错，沼泽遗体。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so, you know, in general, I think bogs are portrayed as these kind of dark, scary places, as we've seen throughout this.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以，你知道，总的来说，正如我们通篇所看到的，沼泽被描绘成这种黑暗、可怕的地方。

sentences.en: And, like, usually there is some truth to that.
sentences.zh: 而且，通常这也有一定道理。

sentences.en: Like, they are hard to walk through, and you can get stuck in the mud, and there are weird gases.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们很难步行穿过，你可能会陷在泥里，而且还有奇怪的气体。

sentences.en: So it's like a caricature based in some amount of real accurate details of what it's like,
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一幅漫画，建立在对真实情况的某些准确细节之上，

sentences.en: but it also falls really short in fully appreciating them for the incredible places that they are.
sentences.zh: 但它在真正充分欣赏它们作为令人惊叹的地方这一点上，也远远不够全面。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I have to admit, bogs are, like, my favorite ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以我必须承认，沼泽就像是我最喜欢的生态系统。

sentences.en: I think they're so cool.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们太酷了。

sentences.en: I used to study botany in the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 我过去常常在中西部研究植物学。

sentences.en: There's much more bogs.
sentences.zh: 那里有更多的沼泽。

sentences.en: There's no bogs here, really, on the West Coast to speak of, but there's real bogs there.
sentences.zh: 西海岸这里真的没有什么值得一提的沼泽，但那里有真正的沼泽。

sentences.en: I like a cranberry bog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢蔓越莓沼泽。

sentences.en: I like a quaking bog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢浮沼。

sentences.en: I mean, a quaking bog is, like, where the sphagnum grows so thick that trees can grow on it, and if you get enough people, they can jump on the sphagnum,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，浮沼是指苔藓长得如此之厚，以至于树木可以在上面生长，如果你聚起足够多的人，他们可以在苔藓上跳跃，

sentences.en: and trees can sway from you jumping on the ground.
sentences.zh: 树木会随着你在地面的跳跃而摇晃。

sentences.en: It is, like, bogs are amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真的是，沼泽太神奇了。

sentences.en: I love them.
sentences.zh: 我爱死它们了。

sentences.en: And then that immediately became an impossibility with the COVID situation.
sentences.zh: 然后这随着新冠疫情的情况立即变得不可能了。

sentences.en: But can I share one cool bog fact that I didn't get to work into the story?
sentences.zh: 但我能分享一个我没能塞进故事里的很酷的沼泽冷知识吗？

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 尽管说吧。

sentences.en: So did you know that bogs breathe?
sentences.zh: 你知道沼泽会呼吸吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不知道。

sentences.en: I did not know that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: So there's this common phenomenon in peatland science called bog breathing.
sentences.zh: 所以泥炭地科学中有一个常见的现象叫做沼泽呼吸。

sentences.en: And what we mean by that is that the surface of a bog, the surface of the vegetation layer, moves up and down.
sentences.zh: 我们的意思是，沼泽的表面，植被层的表面，在上下移动。

sentences.en: It expands or it shrinks depending on the hydrology and where the water table is sitting.
sentences.zh: 它根据水文和地下水位的位置而膨胀或收缩。

sentences.en: And this is actually an adaptive trait.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个适应性特征。

sentences.en: It means when conditions are wet, the water table adjusts, and the whole peat layer adjusts to that shift.
sentences.zh: 这意味着当条件湿润时，地下水位会调整，整个泥炭层也会适应这种变化。

sentences.en: When things get dry, again, that peat layer responds.
sentences.zh: 当情况变干时，泥炭层也会做出反应。

sentences.en: So it's not really breathing that's in, like, respiration.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是那种像呼吸作用一样的呼吸。

sentences.en: It's more like a metaphor of movement when they say bog breathing.
sentences.zh: 当他们说沼泽呼吸时，它更像是一种运动的隐喻。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: It's almost like, I, like, think of it as, like, the bog is, like, a giant's belly that's, like, rising and falling as the ecosystem sort of breathes in and out.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像，我，我想象它就像沼泽是一个巨人的肚子，随着生态系统的一呼一吸而起伏。

sentences.en: It takes on more space and kind of pushes up to the sky, almost like your diaphragm would expand when you're taking a deep breath.
sentences.zh: 它占据了更多的空间，几乎像你的横膈膜在深呼吸时会扩张一样向上推向天空。

sentences.en: But then that can also contract down and that breath is then expelled.
sentences.zh: 但随后它也会收缩下来，然后那口气就被呼出了。

sentences.en: And, you know, this isn't a new phenomenon like scientists have known about bog breathing for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这并不是什么新现象，科学家们很早就知道沼泽呼吸了。

sentences.en: But it's incredibly difficult to measure.
sentences.zh: 但它极难测量。

sentences.en: So this is Roxanne Anderson again.
sentences.zh: 所以这位又是罗克珊·安德森。

sentences.en: So if you think about it, trying to go and measure how much the surface moves up and down, and that's in the order of millimeters.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你仔细想想，试图去测量表面上下移动了多少，那可是毫米级别的。

sentences.en: You know, if you try to measure that by walking onto the bog, which is an unstable and wobbly surface, it's going to be very difficult.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你试图通过走到沼泽上去测量，那是一个不稳定且摇晃的表面，将会非常困难。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It's like, it's like trying to, you measure the surface of a waterbed, you know, like it constantly moves underneath your feet.
sentences.zh: 这就像，这就像你试图测量水床的表面，你知道的，它在你的脚下不断移动。

sentences.en: That's, that must be really frustrating if you're trying to measure it.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图去测量它，那一定令人非常沮丧。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: And so Roxanne Anderson and her colleagues have been looking at ways that they could measure this without actually going out and trying to measure the surface manually.
sentences.zh: 所以罗克珊·安德森和她的同事们一直在寻找方法，可以在不亲自出去手动测量表面的情况下测量这一点。

sentences.en: And what we've been looking at is using a satellite that uses radar.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在研究的是使用带有雷达的卫星。

sentences.en: So basically using radar from a satellite to send a signal down to the bog every few days and getting measurements on how that surface level is changing over time.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上是利用卫星雷达每隔几天向沼泽发送一次信号，并获得关于表面高度随时间变化的测量数据。

sentences.en: What Roxanne and her colleagues have been trying to figure out is like,
sentences.zh: 罗克珊和她的同事们一直试图弄清楚的是，

sentences.en: can they use that bog breathing pattern from the satellite data as a indicator of the overall health of the peatland?
sentences.zh: 他们能否将卫星数据中的这种沼泽呼吸模式用作泥炭地整体健康的指标？

sentences.en: It's like a, it's like a doctor putting a stethoscope to your back and saying, deep breath.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，这就像医生把听诊器贴在你的背上说，深吸一口气。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: And, and, and, you know, I think gathering that data could help scientists understand whether a peatland is functioning as a healthy peatland and a robust carbon sink,
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，而且，你知道，我认为收集这些数据可以帮助科学家了解泥炭地是作为一个健康的泥炭地和一个强健的碳汇在运作，

sentences.en: or whether it's degraded in some way that you maybe didn't know and, and might be actually emitting carbon.
sentences.zh: 还是它以某种你可能不知道的方式退化了，并且实际上可能在排放碳。

sentences.en: So, so what's the pattern they're finding?
sentences.zh: 那么，那么他们发现的模式是什么？

sentences.en: And like, like, how do you tell if the breathing of a bog is healthy or not?
sentences.zh: 并且，如何判断沼泽的呼吸是否健康？

sentences.en: Yeah, I asked Roxanne that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我问过罗克珊。

sentences.en: So what we found is that kind of healthy peatland, if you like, they have one peak and one trough roughly every year.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的是，健康的泥炭地，如果你愿意的话，它们大约每年有一个峰和一个谷。

sentences.en: And the peak is usually, if they're really healthy, it's usually going to be in the autumn with quite a high amplitude.
sentences.zh: 如果它们非常健康，峰值通常会出现在秋季，并且具有相当高的振幅。

sentences.en: And then the trough is going to be in the, in the spring.
sentences.zh: 然后谷值会出现在春季。

sentences.en: So you have this kind of cycle of peaks and troughs.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有这种峰谷交替的循环。

sentences.en: So one, one big breath in and one big breath out every year.
sentences.zh: 也就是每年一次大吸气和一次大呼气。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对，对，对。

sentences.en: And then the more degraded it gets, the more it just becomes kind of no, no peaks, no troughs, just kind of a flatter line.
sentences.zh: 然后它退化得越厉害，就越变得没有什么峰、没有什么谷，只是一条比较平坦的线。

sentences.en: Well, you don't want to see a flat line like a, like an EKG.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你可不想看到像心电图那样的平坦直线。

sentences.en: You don't want that.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不想看到那个。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And, you know, Roxanne says that this new way of gathering bog breathing data is actually like really important or could be really,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，罗克珊说这种收集沼泽呼吸数据的新方法实际上非常重要，或者可能非常重要，

sentences.en: really important for peatland conservation globally.
sentences.zh: 对全球泥炭地保护而言真的非常重要。

sentences.en: I think that the interesting thing for me about this is that it completely changes the way that we can understand peatland globally, because we can just do that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对我来说，这件事最有趣的地方在于它彻底改变了我们全球理解泥炭地的方式，因为我们轻而易举就能做到这一点。

sentences.en: You know, if we spend the time to do the validation like we've done here for any type of peatland,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们花时间像这里这样，对任何类型的泥炭地进行验证，

sentences.en: you might end up with knowing what the signal or the breathing pattern for a particular type of peatland is.
sentences.zh: 你最终可能会了解某种特定类型泥炭地的信号或呼吸模式是什么样的。

sentences.en: And you might be able to detect anomalies that are, you know, diagnostic of degradation for peatlands that, you know, that are impossible to reach or very, very difficult to reach,
sentences.zh: 而且你也许能够检测出各种异常现象，这些现象可以诊断出泥炭地的退化，而这些泥炭地你知道是无法到达的，或者非常、非常难以到达的，

sentences.en: that are really remote or impossible to visit on a regular basis.
sentences.zh: 它们极其偏远，或者根本无法经常去实地探访。

sentences.en: And this is really important because, like, you know, so many peatlands are in these remote locations.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常重要，因为，你看，许多泥炭地都位于这些偏远地区。

sentences.en: And they're places that humans have tended to avoid.
sentences.zh: 而且它们都是人类通常会避开的地方。

sentences.en: And we're actually still discovering new peatlands.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们至今仍在不断发现新的泥炭地。

sentences.en: And often they're really hard to access.
sentences.zh: 而且它们通常都极其难以接近。

sentences.en: And so it could be this really helpful tool in mapping and understanding the role that peatlands are playing as carbon sinks or as carbon sources.
sentences.zh: 因此，这可能是一个非常实用的工具，有助于绘制地图并理解泥炭地作为碳汇或碳源所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that I think is really interesting about the story is that the peatlands are doing a lot of good if they're healthy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这个故事非常有趣的一点是，泥炭地如果保持健康，就会发挥巨大的积极作用。

sentences.en: But if they're not healthy, they're actually kind of a problem because they release that carbon that they've stored.
sentences.zh: 但如果它们不健康，其实就会带来一些麻烦，因为它们会释放出所储存的碳。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's, like, super important that we find out where they are and monitor them and really are invested in keeping them healthy all around the world.
sentences.zh: 而且，找出它们在哪里、监测它们，并真正致力于维持世界各地泥炭地的健康，这超级重要。

sentences.en: Like, it's, like, all of our well-being is sort of caught up in that carbon beneath these hot spots all over the world.
sentences.zh: 可以说，我们所有人的福祉都与世界各地这些热点地区地表下的碳息息相关。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，太酷了。

sentences.en: Well, I love Boggs even more now.
